newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Penn, Larsen named in NZ cricket team.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Penn, Larsen named in NZ cricket team.

text.p: DUNEDIN, March 11 - Central Districts allrounder Andrew Penn and Wellington's Gavin Larsen were on Tuesday named as additions to the New Zealand squad for the second cricket test against Sri Lanka in Hamilton, NZPA reports.
Penn, 22, and Larsen have been brought in following injuries which have ruled out Geoff Allott and placed his fellow fast bowler Heath Davis in doubt for the match starting on Friday.

Chris Harris has been dropped from the squad after being called in on the morning of the first day of the first test in Dunedin last Friday to act as 12th man following Allott's withdrawal with a back injury.
Penn is a newcomer to the national side while veteran medium pacer Larsen has played eight tests but has not been wanted in the test arena so far this season.
Allott's immediate future remains unclear. He broke down at training last Thursday in considerable back pain and it was initially feared he had suffered a stress fracture.
He is to undergo bone scans in Christchurch this week to determine the full extent of the injury.
Davis, the Wellington fast bowler reintroduced to the test attack during last month's series against England, struggled against Sri Lanka in Dunedin with achilles tendon and knee injuries.
Team physiotherapist Mark Plummer gives Davis an 80 percent chance of being fully fit by Friday.
Penn finds himself promoted to the New Zealand side after an outstanding season in which he has been one of the leading wicket-takers in the Shell Trophy competition.
He has taken 34 wickets this summer at an average of just 15.97.
"Andrew is the most consistent performer in Shell Trophy cricket this season," national selection panel convener Ross Dykes said this morning.
The panel had "continued its policy of selecting on form and Andrew's record speaks for itself".
Penn made his first-class debut for Central Districts in 1994-95. He attended the New Zealand Cricket Academy in Christchurch last winter and played for an Academy 11 against Zimbabwe last season.
Penn was in the New Zealand A team to play Sri Lanka in Gisborne early last week but did not bowl a ball when rain saw the match abandoned without play.
Larsen rejoined the squad as an experienced campaigner, Dykes said.
"His qualities are well known and his ability to exploit seaming pitches provides yet another option."
Dykes said the Hamilton pitch had given considerable assistance to the bowlers this season and the selectors thought it wise to cover all the necessary bowling options.
The late withdrawal of Allott meant New Zealand went into the first test with only two strike bowlers in Simon Doull and Davis.

Their backup consisted of medium pacers Matt Horne and Nathan Astle, both of whom at best can be regarded as handy change bowlers at test level, while spinners Dipak Patel and Daniel Vettori were largely disappointing.
New Zealand won the test by an innings and 36 runs after amassing a mammoth 586 for seven declared in their only innings, thanks chiefly to a magnificent unbeaten 267 from Bryan Young.

New Zealand squad: Stephen Fleming (captain), Blair Pocock, Bryan Young, Matt Horne, Nathan Astle, Chris Cairns, Adam Parore, Daniel Vettori, Dipak Patel, Heath Davis, Simon Doull, Andrew Penn, Gavin Larsen.
